items.title: 68533_Sam Jones oral history interview
items.q: You've got your great Donald Byrd, the Black Byrds. And if you tell me that the music that Donald Byrd is playing is jazz music--then, man, I might as well get out of the business, you know.

ctx.x: Um, um, well I can't see where you got to put--I get back to ah, what I was saying. I wrote music man, see--this music-the black man's music I'm speaking of-now, you see, those guys are playing the white man's music because the white man is making--he's the man that's making the money, you see? He's sitting in his lavishly apart--um, um office on Park Avenue, you know, uh, Hollywood Boulevard in California, or somewhere else, some big office in London or somewhere uh, with his Rolls Royce and chauffeur downstairs…

music. This is not the music that you want to play, but you are ordered to play that. It's the same as therefore when Columbia starts signing, you know, all the musicians if you remember when all this kind of--this is not, uh, their choice, you know? Sure, he hand them out about ten grand, here we just want you to sign--$10,000, $10,000, $10,000, $10,000--we want you to sign. At one time when I saw these guys that are--that have never seen $10,000 all at once in their life, yeah, you know, you jump at it. And…
